reasoning: B2 is proposed as an explicit course editorial choice: the exact noun is B2 in the inspected CEFR-J v1.5 headword/POS list and is taught in a B1-B2 workplace lesson. Oxford labels its selected presence topics C1, so the new evidence does not make the sense unanimously or dictionary-certified B2. The existing original definition/example fit ordinary presence, not a paper record or crowd headcount.
preserved: Stable ID, definition, example, forms, memberships, image/audio/morphology/domain gates, practice modes, and all expressions remain unchanged. This proposal does not itself mark language reviewed.

sources.label_scope: Working life and Education topics attached to the ordinary presence sense.
sources.observation: Sense 1 concerns presence at a place and includes recording students attendance; sense 2 separately concerns headcount. Selected C1 is retained as conflicting evidence.
Selected uncountable sense covers being present at an event or regular participation in an institution; the headcount meaning is separately listed. No selected CEFR label was observed.

Public publisher overview explicitly teaches attendance-policy vocabulary and workplace absence communication at B1-B2. Only the overview was inspected; subscriber worksheets and videos were not acquired.
